title: 4.2 A 1.8-to-3.0GHz Fully Integrated All-In-One CMOS Frequency Management Module Achieving -47/+42ppm Inaccuracy from -40 to 95°C and -150/+70ppm After Accelerated Aging
problem: Wireless/wired communication systems require stable frequency references, traditionally using bulky off-chip crystals. On-chip RC-based references struggle with poor aging performance (>±1030 ppm drift after aging even with redundancy) and inadequate frequency accuracy for modern protocols; integrating on-chip reference into synthesizer for true FMM remains unachieved.
motivation: IoT and cost-sensitive applications need crystal-free, fully integrated frequency management to reduce BOM size/cost while meeting protocol accuracy and stability specs.
method: A frequency management module puts an RC-based frequency reference (a resistor-capacitor oscillator with stability improvements) and a frequency synthesizer (a circuit that generates different output frequencies) on the same CMOS chip. The oscillator stays accurate within ±47/±42 parts per million across -40 to +95°C. The synthesizer generates frequencies from 1.8 to 3.0 GHz with this accuracy; after accelerated aging tests, accuracy drops to ±150/±70 parts per million.
key_novelty: An RC frequency reference (resistor-capacitor oscillator) and synthesizer (frequency-generation circuit) are integrated on a single CMOS chip for the first time, achieving frequency stability matching external crystal oscillators and eliminating off-chip frequency trim (tuning).
contributions: Fully integrated FMM (reference + synthesizer) on single chip replaces external crystal
±47/±42 ppm inaccuracy -40 to +95°C (unprecedented for on-chip RC-based reference)
±150/±70 ppm post-aging specs, ~7x better than prior RC-core designs
1.8–3.0 GHz output suitable for IoT wireless/wired protocols
baselines: Prior RC-core on-chip references (±1030 ppm aging drift)
limitations: Phase noise, jitter specs, and power consumption not discussed.
